body: SOCOM U.S. Navy SEALs is Zipper Interactive's PlayStation 2 tactical shooter, first released in North America on 27 August 2002. The player leads a small team through military operations viewed from behind the controlled soldier. Success depends on the squad's movement and instructions as well as individual aim. A bundled USB headset gives commands another form: the player can speak to the team during the single-player campaign. The game places communication within the action, making the role of commander something performed through both the controller and the player's own voice.

Twelve offline missions give the squad a succession of objectives that reward deliberate approaches. Orders allow teammates to contribute instead of leaving every task to the controlled character. The player has to consider where the group is moving and how an instruction changes the next encounter. Speech recognition through the headset adds an unusual physical connection to those decisions. A command is spoken while attention remains on the field, giving the operation a different rhythm from repeatedly opening a menu to direct soldiers who stand outside the player's immediate view.

Online play used the same headset for voice chat between human teammates, making coordination part of the original PlayStation 2 network experience. SOCOM was the console's first game to use that accessory. David Sears directed the project and Jeremy Soule composed its music. European and Australian editions followed in 2003, alongside the wider development of console online services. The original servers eventually closed in 2012. Its place in that history comes from making conversation useful during the match, connecting a peripheral on the player's head to cooperation between people in different rooms.
